faculty.name: Prof. Rakesh Tiwari
faculty.research_interests: Forest ecology, Photosynthesis, Photorespiration, agricultural greenhouse gas mitigation
modules_taught: agricultural greenhouse gas mitigation and monitoring
faculty.biography: My work focuses on photosynthesis, photorespiration and how plants respond to warming. Alongside teaching and developing university-wide courses, I support researchers across disciplines through training in digital tools and advanced research methods. I guide PhD and master’s student projects and contribute to long-term forest monitoring and photosynthetic heat-tolerance measurements in Bhadra Reserve Forest, alongside related field and laboratory collaborations in Goa and elsewhere.

faculty.name: Dr. Harisha M. N.
faculty.research_interests: Wildlife ecology, biodiversity assessment, ornithology, butterfly diversity, wildlife conservation
faculty.biography: Working in the field of wildlife management at Kuvempu University, Karnataka, India, my academic and research interests encompass wildlife ecology, biodiversity assessment, ornithology, butterfly diversity, and wildlife conservation. I bring over five years of field research experience and specialized expertise in identifying birds and mammals through their calls and vocalisations. Passionate about wildlife research, conservation, and practical field-based training for students, my teaching and research activities aim to advance biodiversity documentation, deepen ecological understanding, and contribute to the preservation of wildlife habitats.
faculty.additional_notes: My research interests focus on wildlife ecology, biodiversity assessment, and conservation. I am keen to collaborate on interdisciplinary research projects, contribute to scientific publications, and support field-based learning and conservation initiatives.

faculty.name: Prof. Vijaya Kumara
faculty.research_interests: Wildlife ecology, biodiversity conservation, human–wildlife interactions
faculty.biography: I am a dedicated academician with a strong passion for wildlife conservation, teaching, research, and academic administration. My areas of interest include wildlife ecology, biodiversity conservation, and human–wildlife interactions. I am committed to fostering academic excellence, inspiring young researchers, and promoting scientific understanding and sustainable wildlife conservation through education, research, and community engagement.
